reviewNotes: On 2026-07-25 Carlos stated that he created all of this material and chose MIT for the repository code. Authorship of the eight local media files is therefore recorded as owned.

The safest launch path approved the ownership-recorded Observatory poster for public production display while keeping monogram sheets, videos, and multi-ten-megabyte GLBs excluded from runtime until accessibility and optimization work is complete.
MIT covers portfolio code; it does not auto-import binary media into the live site. Every imagesandvideo path remains excluded from runtime source imports.
The site-level content gate compares this register to the actual imagesandvideo directory, byte lengths, and SHA-256 hashes so later additions or substitutions cannot silently bypass review.

On 2026-07-27 Carlos supplied the gold CA²M monogram and asked for it to be integrated into the portfolio. That request grants mark-only runtime clearance: the register status moves to runtime-approved, imagesandvideo/logo.png moves to include as the derivation source, and every other local file keeps its exclude decision. The full legal-name lockup image stays unpublished. On 2026-08-11 Carlos confirmed his full legal name and approved it as the site's public identity copy, so the runtime identity became "Carlos Alfredo Carpio Meza" as text; that decision does not clear the raster wordmark sheet, which still needs its own review.

On 2026-07-27 Carlos also approved the robot water video as the homepage hero’s moving visual. Its runtime derivative is muted (audio track removed), scaled to 1440×810, keyframe-dense, and hash-pinned with its poster; the raw MP4 stays outside runtime imports like every other imagesandvideo source.
